_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 12 rendered pages (idx 0-11 = printed folios 1-12), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB4/3, SET-1, Q.P. Code 57/3/1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 12 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The tops of all odd indices were checked at full width in one montage: idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 3 Hindi Q3, idx 5 Hindi Section B / Q7, idx 7 Hindi Q12(a), idx 9 Hindi Q13(b) passage, so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 11 (folio 12) is blank apart from an asterisk and the footer. The paper is a scan and was read by vision only. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q6, Q11 and Q13 (four alternatives). Q12 prints (a) and (b) with NO OR between them and the scheme marks both (1/2 x 3 + 1 1/2 = 3), so Q12 is one row. Q13(a) is a case study with three sub-parts, one row each, carrying the scheme's split 2/2/1. Its OR, Q13(b), replaces the WHOLE case study with a DIFFERENT case study (a gene-therapy passage with its own sub-parts (i)-(iii), scheme split 1/3/1), so it is ONE row Q13b, alternative to Q13ai, with its own passage in context and its own setId (CS2), the shape of 2022 57/2/1 Q13b. The generic lead-in 'Read the paragraph given below and answer the questions that follow :' (Q13(a)) and 'Read the following paragraph and answer the questions that follow :' (Q13(b)) are instructions, not passage, and are left out of context. Quotes straightened (Q11(a), Q11(b) and Q13(b) print curly double quotes; Q12(a) curly single quotes), scientific names plain (Rhizobium, Anabaena, Trichoderma, Baculovirus; Thermus aquaticus and E.coli are printed underlined and carried as plain text, E.coli without a space as printed). Typos kept as printed: Q1 'straight entered', Q4 'Organic farmer use', Q8 'excess mucous', Q10(a) 'South Americal jungle', Q13(a) passage 'Taq polymerase, is extracted'. No question asks the student to draw, so no _drawFigure. Q5 examines content the rationalised syllabus removed (organism and its environment), so it carries _outOfSyllabus.

questions.stem: A boy developed some allergic reactions when he straight entered into his air conditioned room after a game of football outside his house. Write any two symptoms that could be noticed in such condition. How does our body combat such conditions ?

(i) Write the Scientific name of the plant from where natural cannabinoids are obtained.
(ii) Mention the parts of the plant that are used for extracting the drug.
(iii) How does the drug affect human body ?
Epithelial lining of our intestine is considered as secondary lymphoid organ. Justify the statement.

Farmers are often suggested to use the following organisms in their crop land so as to improve the soil fertility.
(i) Rhizobium (ii) Anabaena
Explain.
Organic farmer use Trichoderma and Baculovirus as biological control agents. Explain.

questions._outOfSyllabus: Organism and its environment: responses to abiotic factors (thermoregulation, the surface area to volume ratio of small animals, hibernation and migration), removed from the rationalised NCERT chapter. questions.stem: Mammals are capable of maintaining homeostasis. But, very few smaller animals can survive in polar regions. Give reasons.

Observe the schematic representation given above and answer the following questions :
(i) Identify A and B.
(ii) Calculate the growth rate of bacteria in a curd sample, where 1 million bacteria increased to two million, within a period of one hour.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a schematic of a box labelled Population D, with an arrow labelled Immigration at the top and an arrow labelled Emigration at the bottom, and two circled labels joined to the box by arrows, B on the left and A on the right. Which of A and B points into the box and which points out of it decides the answer to (i), so the arrow directions are withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem: Identify the type of pyramid given above. Write the identifying feature on the basis of which you identified it.

questions._flag: Ordinary marking latitude, not a void: the scheme accepts either ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, antigen-antibody interaction) or PCR (polymerase chain reaction, early detection by amplifying the pathogen's genetic material) for part (a). The solution teaches ELISA and names PCR as the scheme's accepted alternative.
questions.stem:
(a) Write the complete name of the diagnostic test for AIDS. Explain the principle it works on.

(c) Write your suggestions to the patient to avoid infection in future.

(b) What is elution ? State the importance of elution in this process.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a rectangle drawn as a gel with four lanes numbered 1 to 4 (bottom to top), each starting from an open rectangular well at the left and carrying a row of vertical band marks; circled labels P, Q and R point down into lane 4 from above, a circled label T points up into lane 1 from below, and the left and right edges are marked 'end' with circled labels U (left) and S (right). Which feature each letter marks, and so which end is the anode, decides part (a) and is withheld here. Page idx 8.

questions.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
questions.context: Enzyme Taq polymerase, is extracted from a eubacterial microorganism Thermus aquaticus from Yellowstone National Park in Montana, USA and isolated by Chien et al. (1976). Taq polymerase successfully replaced the DNA polymerase from E.coli that was being used in PCR earlier and this shift revolutionised the PCR technique.
questions.stem: Taq polymerase after its discovery replaced E.coli DNA polymerase in PCR technique. Explain giving reasons why was the need felt for the change ?
